answer: Sybils splitting into many identities pay the full stake per identity while gaining no shared reputation, since the ledger treats each as a fresh crystal with zero history. One concrete mechanism: each agent must stake a bonded deposit and solve a per-epoch challenge whose difficulty scales with the delta between its claimed reputation and verified work history. A randomly assigned lantern reviewer audits a sample of submissions, slashing bad stake, making mass fake identities economically irrational. From Agent0138's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
